data.body:
=== RED TEST FIRST, BY OPERATOR DIRECTION — AND IT IS RED AGAINST BOTH WRONG STATES OF THE CODE ===

`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_parent_clear_requires_peer_evidence.py`, committed as
**ea552f8589** on branch `fix-88d9-peer-evidence` (based on the revert `2241e3d189`). Three cells, all
driving the production entry point `compute_inbound_mutations` — never a private helper, so a moved or
missing helper reads as a failed ASSERTION rather than an AttributeError (the reverted change had
shuffled this logic between modules twice).

**MEASURED, both directions — this is the part that matters:**

  against the DEFECTIVE tree (gerrit/main @ 6baa030460, the code that caused the incident):
    FAILED test_a_parent_the_peer_never_had_is_not_cleared
      "REGRESSION -- the 63-ticket incident. A local parent rebar never pushed was cleared because it
       is in managed_refs (emitted parent_id=None)"
    1 failed, 2 passed

  against the REVERTED tree (2241e3d189, what will be on main):
    FAILED test_a_parent_the_peer_once_had_is_cleared
      "the peer's last-synced parent was DC-9 and the peer now has NONE"
    1 failed, 2 passed

So each WRONG state satisfies one half and fails the other:
 * defective  = clears a parent the peer never had  -> fails the negative cell;
 * reverted   = never clears at all                 -> fails the positive cell.
**A single assertion cannot distinguish "correct" from "one of the two failure modes."** That is
exactly how this repo has shipped oracles that could not fail (2944, 59b2, the vacuous `08-assign`
cell), and it is why the pair must not be split or trimmed to make a build green. The third cell —
`test_an_unobserved_parent_is_never_cleared_even_with_peer_evidence` — holds the fail-open read safe:
with peer evidence present, an ABSENT `parent` key must still emit nothing, because `get_parent_map`
degrades to `{}` on any REST failure and a truncated page walk simply omits issues.

--- THE FIX THE THIRD STATE REQUIRES ---

Clear only on POSITIVE evidence that the peer once carried this parent. The evidence channel is the
ADR-0026 per-binding record, which already exists, is already advanced every pass, and is already
persisted by the binding-store commit path with no new commit surface:

 1. `binding_store`: `set_peer_parent(local_id, key)` / `get_peer_parent(local_id)` on the binding
    entry — its OWN key, NOT a 6th entry in `_BASELINE_FIELDS` (that tuple is the 5-scalar
    three-way-merge vocabulary consumed by `outbound_field_diff` and `binding_walk`; widening it would
    perturb that merge). Absent = unknown = fail safe, matching the documented baseline semantics
    ("an ABSENT baseline is VALID and degrades to local-wins").
 2. `reconcile`: advance it beside `_advance_baselines` (`reconcile.py:519-536`) — **only when this
    pass OBSERVED the parent key.** This is the load-bearing detail: if a fail-open read were allowed
    to overwrite a good history with "no parent", the next pass would read that as a deletion and the
    incident returns by a longer route.
 3. `inbound_fields.diff_inbound_parent`: emit the clear only when `get_peer_parent` returns a truthy
    key AND this pass observed no parent. `managed_refs` may stay as an additional gate but must never
    DECIDE — it cannot answer the question, which is the whole lesson of this incident and of 2b16.

Same shape as the arbitration 2b16 needs. One wrong premise produced two defects; one evidence channel
retires both.

--- STATUS ---
Revert 1292 has `LLM-Review +1` and is awaiting `Verified`; the production bridge stays DISABLED until
it lands. The fix is NOT pushed: a RED-only change cannot earn `Verified +1`, so it squashes with the
implementation. The store repair is settled — operator ACCEPTED the current state for the 61 closed
tickets; the two that were not closed (437c in_progress, bf03 open) were repaired with a plain
`rebar edit --parent` and verified. The missing capability is filed as idea 5992-f317-e05e-42f7
(dedicated `parent` verb with `--force`), out of scope by operator direction.
